metadata.goal: Investigate the most unusual trajectories in the provided NYC data and explain how they differ from the dominant patterns in the collection.
metadata.dataset_description: A point-level derived WorldTrace case containing 24 car trajectories: 21 ordinary urban comparison trajectories and three explicitly named deviations. The CSV exposes coordinates, timestamps, point-level speed, average speed, and traveled distance.
metadata.speed_derivation: GPS haversine distances and timestamp differences; no independent speed input. First point speed uses first outgoing segment, later points use incoming segments.

insight_list.insight: wt03_trajectory_22 and wt03_trajectory_23 differ from the typical patterns: their average speeds are much higher, while wt03_trajectory_24 differs from the others because the traveled distance is the longest and much longer than the others.

plot.title: Speed and Distance Exceptions
plot.description: Separate plots show that wt03_trajectory_22 and wt03_trajectory_23 are speed exceptions and wt03_trajectory_24 is the distance exception relative to 21 ordinary comparison trajectories.

insight_list.question: Which trajectories differ from the dominant pattern in average speed or traveled distance?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Use the speed plot to identify wt03_trajectory_22 and wt03_trajectory_23 and the distance plot to identify wt03_trajectory_24 before examining their route geometry.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
df=pd.read_csv(dataset_path)
derived=[]
for tid,g in df.groupby('trajectory_id'):
    g=g.sort_values('point_index');x=np.radians(g.longitude.to_numpy());y=np.radians(g.latitude.to_numpy())
    a=np.sin(np.diff(y)/2)**2+np.cos(y[:-1])*np.cos(y[1:])*np.sin(np.diff(x)/2)**2
    km=6371.0088*2*np.arcsin(np.sqrt(np.clip(a,0,1)))
    seconds=pd.to_datetime(g.timestamp,format='mixed').diff().dt.total_seconds().to_numpy()[1:]
    derived.append({'trajectory_id':tid,'distance_meters':float(km.sum()*1000),'avg_speed_kmh':float(km.sum()/seconds.sum()*3600)})
summary=pd.DataFrame(derived)
print(summary.sort_values('avg_speed_kmh',ascending=False))

insight_list.insight: wt03_trajectory_22 and wt03_trajectory_23 have average speeds over 80 km/h, start from the same broad South Brooklyn area, and end in the same broad South Brooklyn destination area, but their observed road-following trajectories are very different.

plot.title: Road-Following Route and Speed Comparison
plot.description: Fixed road-following GPS paths and point speeds computed from adjacent GPS distances and timestamp differences; average speeds use total GPS path length / elapsed time. Region strings are descriptive labels.

insight_list.question: Do wt03_trajectory_22 and wt03_trajectory_23 combine similarly high speeds with the same broad start and destination areas despite following different road corridors?
insight_list.actionable_insight: The route and speed comparison separates high speed from route geometry: wt03_trajectory_22 and wt03_trajectory_23 share broad endpoints but not the same road path or point-level speed profile.

derived=[]
for tid,g in df.groupby('trajectory_id'):
    g=g.sort_values('point_index');x=np.radians(g.longitude.to_numpy());y=np.radians(g.latitude.to_numpy())
    a=np.sin(np.diff(y)/2)**2+np.cos(y[:-1])*np.cos(y[1:])*np.sin(np.diff(x)/2)**2
    km=6371.0088*2*np.arcsin(np.sqrt(np.clip(a,0,1)))
    seconds=pd.to_datetime(g.timestamp,format='mixed').diff().dt.total_seconds().to_numpy()[1:]
    derived.append({'trajectory_id':tid,'distance_meters':float(km.sum()*1000),'avg_speed_kmh':float(km.sum()/seconds.sum()*3600)})
summary=pd.DataFrame(derived)

insight_list.evidence: Both average and point-wise speed derive from GPS and timestamps. point_index only orders rows; region labels do not add native inputs.

insight_list.insight: wt03_trajectory_24 avoids the NYC urban core for most of its route, which leads to its longest traveled distance while its start and end remain in the city.
